Lucas Daniel Duarte Cabral

Back-end Developer · Java 21 · Spring Boot · PostgreSQL · RabbitMQ · Docker
Open-source contributor in C/C++ and Vulkan (emulation and static recompilation)
Systems Analysis and Development student at UCDB · Campo Grande, MS, Brazil (UTC−4)
Open to back-end internships and junior developer roles — on-site, remote or international

About me

I build back-end services with Java 21 and Spring Boot, and I focus on what keeps software correct under load: automated tests against real infrastructure, concurrency control, asynchronous messaging and containerized delivery.

  • Recently shipped: closed 6 IDOR (broken access control) issues and added Testcontainers integration tests, Swagger/OpenAPI and Flyway migrations to ASUS RPG Platform
  • Building: DKB Recomp, a static recompilation of a Switch 2 game to native Windows with Vulkan
  • Learning: Kafka, cloud deployment and observability
  • Education: Systems Analysis and Development, Universidade Católica Dom Bosco (UCDB), 2024 – 2027
  • Languages: Portuguese (native) · English (B1, intermediate)

Open source

DKB Recomp: creator and maintainer

  • Static recompilation of Donkey Kong Bananza (Switch 2) into a native Windows x86-64 executable with a Vulkan renderer: the ARM64 code is translated to C ahead of time, with no emulator at run time
  • All 4,820 Ampere shader stages of the first 3D scene are lowered and translated to SPIR-V; the game boots, renders the tutorial and answers the controller
  • 900+ stars and 49 forks; I set the repository up for contributors (per-task issues, roadmap, testing guide) and have reviewed and merged 28 PRs from 4 people. No game files are included.

C C++ Python Vulkan SPIR-V

Pull requests merged in other people's projects (26)

  • Shadow of the Colossus PC, native port, C++/Vulkan (15): +6% FPS from the buffer cache, FSR 3 frame generation fixed on AMD RX 7000, textures on GTX 10xx by emulating barycentrics with a geometry shader. I also keep the community fork (30 stars).
  • TotK PC Recomp, C (7): Brazilian Portuguese menu and installer, thread pools sized by the process affinity mask, colour profiles, field of view, 32:9 layouts.
  • shadPS4, PS4 emulator, C++ (3): texture cache lookup, freeing nested indirect buffer frames, DualShock 4 touchpad height.

Featured projects

ASUS RPG Platform — full-stack virtual tabletop

My main project: 160+ commits, continuous deployment on Railway.

  • Spring Boot REST API + WebSocket (STOMP) for real-time play; JWT auth with Spring Security and role-based campaign permissions (owner, game master, player)
  • Security: audited the API and fixed 6 IDOR vulnerabilities so users can only reach their own resources
  • Quality: unit tests (JUnit 5, Mockito), MockMvc API flows and an integration test on real PostgreSQL 17 via Testcontainers; suite grew from 22 to 38 tests; Swagger/OpenAPI docs with JWT Bearer
  • Schema safety: replaced Hibernate ddl-auto=update with Flyway (V1 baseline of the 39-table schema, validate in production)
  • LGPD features (data export, consent, anonymization), audit history and snapshots; React SPA bundled into a single Docker image

Java 21 Spring Boot Spring Security JPA WebSocket React PostgreSQL Flyway Docker

Discord Lyrics Status — desktop app that syncs song lyrics to Discord

  • Detects the song playing on the PC, fetches synced lyrics and updates the Discord status line by line, with a configurable rate limit
  • All-in-one .exe with tray icon and autostart, 12 UI languages (i18n), Spotify API and Android versions
  • CI on GitHub Actions to build the .exe

Python Discord API Spotify API GitHub Actions

Mesa Pronta — Discord bot for scheduling tabletop RPG sessions

  • No double booking: joining locks the session row with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE plus a UNIQUE constraint; a test fires 20 concurrent joins at 1 seat and asserts exactly one succeeds
  • Reliable reminders: a scheduler polls due sessions with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED and publishes 24h/1h reminders to RabbitMQ; the consumer retries 3× with backoff, then parks failures in a dead-letter queue
  • Integration tests with Testcontainers, Docker Compose and CI on GitHub Actions

Java 21 Spring Boot JDA PostgreSQL RabbitMQ Testcontainers Docker

Pix Lite — Pix-style payments API

  • Idempotent transfers: every transfer needs an Idempotency-Key; 20 concurrent requests with the same key produce exactly one debit
  • No deadlocks: both accounts are locked with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE in id order; a test runs 50 threads transferring in both directions and checks that no money is created or lost
  • Ledger-backed statements, RFC 7807 errors, Swagger UI; k6 load test at ~256 req/s with p95 of 257 ms and 0% errors

Java 21 Spring Boot 4 PostgreSQL Flyway Testcontainers k6 Docker

Radar de Vagas — job radar and application tracker

  • Scheduled collection from public job APIs (GitHub Issues, Remotive), with filtering, scoring and URL deduplication
  • Application pipeline with follow-up dates and a REST API; deliberately does not auto-apply, to respect each site's terms of service
  • API clients tested against recorded JSON with MockRestServiceServer, so CI never depends on the network

Java 21 Spring Boot Flyway Docker GitHub Actions

SteamQuest — digital-game e-commerce in PostgreSQL (UCDB team project)

  • Implemented the fn_finalizar_pedido transaction: order locking with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE, status validation, payment creation and order finalization

PostgreSQL PL/pgSQL Git

§1: Summary

I'm a programmer that makes music and writes. I love to learn, solve problems, and create, whether that involves music, artwork, or coding. For work, I build Nibiru, a blockchain built for speed, scale, and ease of use.

⚡ Unique-Divine/jiyuu CLI utilities monorepo solving concrete dev problems: Go coverage merging (gocovmerge), Windows↔Linux encoding fixes (winfixtext), language-agnostic dev commands across Go/Rust/TS (mycli), Markdown TOC generation (mdtoc), and LLM context parsing (aictx). Built primarily in Go with TypeScript components.

§3: Other Passions and Interests

  • 🎼 Music: I practice the 🎷 and 🎹.
  • 🧠 Anki: I'm a huge nerd about spaced repetition software and other strategies for accelerated learning. I've been using Anki to learn faster and remember more of what I learn for probably 5+ years at this point. Although I have over 100,000 mature cards, the reviews take up less than 10 minutes a day when I stop adding new material. Using Anki effectively was a crucial element in my journey to learn Japanese to fluency.

Research

I lead the Computational Multiphase Physics (CoMPhy) Lab at Durham. We study non-Newtonian free-surface flows and soft-matter singularities—drops, bubbles, jets, and sheets where interfaces change rapidly.

Work combines high-fidelity simulation (Basilisk DNS), theory, and collaborative experiments, linking microstructural stress to continuum dynamics and applications in industry and nature. See research.

Latest: Sanjay, V., “Singularities in Soft Matter Systems,” Contemporary Physics (2026).
